title: Product tours talk at buyers. Two-way demos talk with them
summary: Product tours push the same steps at every buyer. A two-way demo answers questions in your real product and turns each one into first-party data.
body_markdown:
**A one-way demo** shows the buyer something your team prepared in advance, in the order you chose. **A two-way demo** listens to the buyer and changes what it shows based on what they ask. Most product tours on SaaS websites today are one-way, and that is why so many of them get clicked through and forgotten.


Think about the last time you sat through a product tour. A tooltip told you to click "Reports". You clicked. Another tooltip, another click. Somewhere around step four you had a real question, maybe whether the tool works with your CRM, and there was nowhere to put it. So you either kept clicking to the end or closed the tab.


That is not a criticism of the teams building tours. Navattic, Storylane, Arcade, Supademo and Consensus made it possible to show a product without booking a call, and for years that was a big step forward. But the format has a ceiling, and buyers have started to hit it.


The same buyer and the same question. The tour keeps playing; Karumi answers it in the product.


## What makes a product tour one-way?


A tour is built once. Someone on your team captures the product, writes the tooltips and decides the order. Every visitor then gets that same sequence, whether they are a CFO looking at approvals or an admin checking SSO.


Three things follow from that:


- **The path is fixed.** You can add branches, but every branch is one you had to predict and build ahead of time.
- **The buyer can't steer.** They can go forward or back. They can't say "show me how this works for a team of 400".
- **You only learn what they clicked.** Completion rate and drop-off step tell you where people lost interest, not why.


A one-way demo is a broadcast. It talks at the buyer, and it is good at that. It just can't listen.


## "But tours have AI agents now"


Fair point, and worth being precise about. In the last year several tour vendors added AI agents on top of their captured demos. Navattic's agent navigates through pre-recorded captures, Storylane's RepX can play a demo or a video during a chat, and Supademo's agent opens the demo, video or doc that matches the question. We went through each of them, with sources, in our post on[live vs pre-recorded AI demo agents](https://karumi.ai/blog/live-vs-pre-recorded-ai-demo-agents) .


These agents do let the buyer ask something. What they can show in reply is still limited to what was captured. If nobody recorded the HubSpot settings page, the agent can describe it, but it can't open it. The conversation became two-way; the product behind it stayed one-way.


## What does a two-way demo look like?


Take the same buyer and the same question: "Does this work with HubSpot?"


In a two-way demo, an agent is running your actual product while it talks. It hears the question, says yes, opens the integrations page and shows the sync settings. If the buyer follows up with "and what happens to deals that already exist?", it goes one level deeper. Nobody wrote that path. The buyer did, by asking.


That is the whole idea behind[Karumi](https://karumi.ai/products/videocall-agent) . The agent joins in about two seconds, shares its screen, and walks the buyer through your real product, not a recording. It learns the product by exploring it, so there is no library of tours to keep up to date when you ship.


## What do you learn from a two-way demo?


This is the part people underestimate. When a buyer talks to your demo, they tell you things a click map never will. Every session gives you first-party data in their own words:


- **The questions they asked** , in order, and what the agent showed in reply.
- **What they are trying to solve** : their use case, team size, timing, and the tools they use today.
- **What held them back** : price concerns, a missing integration, a security review coming up.
- **Who they are** : company, role and whether they fit your ICP.


All of it lands in Salesforce or HubSpot with a summary your rep can read in a minute. Compare that with a tour, where the best signal you get is that someone from a company you can't identify reached step 7 of 12.


That data is also useful well beyond sales. The questions buyers ask most often are a pretty good roadmap for your website copy, your docs and your next feature.


## Do two-way demos actually perform better?


Across Karumi customers, the numbers are hard to ignore:


- **3.2x more meetings** than static assets like videos and tours.
- **12 minutes** per session on average. That is about 6x longer than people watch a product video, and 4x longer than an average ChatGPT session.
- **97% less maintenance** , because the agent updates itself as the product changes instead of waiting for someone to re-capture screens.


The session length is the one that surprised us. Twelve minutes is a long time for anyone to spend on a vendor's website. People stay because the demo keeps answering them.


## When is a tour still the right tool?


Honestly, sometimes. If you want a 30-second teaser on a feature page, or a step-by-step guide for an onboarding email, a short tour does the job and you know exactly what everyone will see. Some teams also need a fully scripted path for regulated industries.


But if the goal is to get a buyer from curious to convinced without waiting for a sales call, the questions are the point. A demo that can't answer them leaves the hardest part of the job to a rep, days later.


## How do you move from a tour to a two-way demo?


Less work than people expect, mainly because there is nothing to export:


1. **Give the agent access to your product** , usually a demo environment with sample data. No tours to rebuild.
2. **Let it learn the flows you demo.** Karumi maps the product and builds the journeys your tours used to cover. Share your best tours and we make sure those flows are in.
3. **Swap the embed.** Same spot on your website, now a live agent. Most teams run both side by side for a while, compare the results, then switch. Most are live in two weeks.


If you are on Navattic, Storylane, Arcade, Supademo or Consensus today, we put together a page on[what switching looks like](https://karumi.ai/migrate) , with a side-by-side of both experiences.


## FAQ


### Is a two-way demo the same as a chatbot?


No. A chatbot answers in text. A two-way demo answers by showing: it opens the screen, clicks through the flow and explains it as it goes.


### Can I keep my existing tours while I try it?


Yes. Most teams run the tour and the agent side by side, look at meetings booked from each, and then decide.


### Does the buyer need a microphone or camera?


No. They can type or talk, and they never need to turn on a camera.


### Where does the first-party data go?


Each session is summarized, scored and synced to Salesforce or HubSpot, with the full transcript available in Karumi.
